question: How has the U.S. regulatory stance on banks engaging in crypto activities shifted over time, and for which activities?
author: authored by Claude (in chat)

program.title: Bank crypto activities: the stance over time
program.thesis: Find every passage about whether banks may engage in crypto-asset or stablecoin activities, classify the activity and how permissive the passage is, and flag reversals of earlier restrictions. Grouping by year and issuer shows the policy swing.

unit.rationale: Substantive paragraphs from bank-regulator letters, the Fed's withdrawal, NYDFS guidance, the executive order, the PWG report, and the GENIUS Act.

doc_notes.note: OCC interpretive letter from July 2020 on national bank authority to provide cryptocurrency custody services.

OCC interpretive letter from November 2021 addressing whether national banks may engage in crypto custody, stablecoin reserve, and node activities, and the supervisory process that applies before they do.

OCC interpretive letter from March 2025 addressing crypto-asset custody, distributed ledger, and stablecoin activities by national banks, including the status of earlier OCC supervisory requirements for these activities.
OCC interpretive letter from May 2025 on crypto-asset custody and execution services by national banks.
Federal Reserve Board press release from April 2025 withdrawing earlier guidance to banks about crypto-asset and dollar token activities.
July 2025 report of the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets; it describes policy history and makes recommendations rather than binding rules.
